00d9e0f9 the `fields` arguments.
00d9e112 For example, to represent the following schema:
00d9e143   Struct(
00d9e14d       a=Int(),

00d9e1fe       "a",
00d9e209       "b:lengths",
00d9e21c       "b:values:lengths",
00d9e236       "b:values:values",
00d9e24f       "c:lengths",
00d9e262       "c:c1",
00d9e270       "c:c2:lengths",
00d9e286       "c:c2:values",
00d9e2a0 And for the following instance of the struct:
00d9e2cf   Struct(

00d9e2e4       b=[[4, 5], [6, 7, 8], [], [9]],

00d9e397       "a": [3],
00d9e3a7       "b:lengths": [4],

00d9e3e7       "b:values:values": [4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9],
00d9e414       "c:lengths": [2],
00d9e42c       "c:c1": ["alex", "bob"],
00d9e44b       "c:c2:lengths": [2, 1],
00d9e469       "c:c2:values", [10, 11, 12],
00d9e491 In general, every field name in the format "{prefix}:lengths" defines a domain
00d9e4e0 "{prefix}", and every subsequent field in the format "{prefix}:{field}" will
00d9e52d be in that domain, and the length of the domain is provided for each entry of
00d9e57b the parent domain. In the example, "b:lengths" defines a domain of length 4, so
00d9e5cb every field under domain "b" will have 4 entries.
00d9e5fd The "lengths" field for a given domain must appear before any reference to
00d9e648 that domain.

00da34fe     the layer computes Y = X * W^T + b, where X has size (M x K),
00da3540     W has size (N x K), b has size (N), and Y has size (M x N),

00da362e     X \in [a_0, a_1, ...,a_{k-1}, a_k, ..., a_{n-1}] where a_i \in N+ and k is
00da367d     the axis provided, then X will be coerced into a 2-dimensional tensor with
00da36cc     dimensions [a_0 * ... * a_{k-1}, a_k * ... * a_{n-1}]. For the default
00da3717     case where axis=1, this means the X tensor will be coerced into a 2D tensor
00da3767     of dimensions [a_0, a_1 * ... * a_{n-1}], where a_0 is often the batch size.

00da3988 Applies 8-bit row-wise quantization by determining the range
00da39c5       (maximum - minimum) and offset (minimum value) of each row in the input
00da3a13       matrix, and then scaling each element to an 8-bit number between 0 and
00da3a60       255. To later de-quantize values, the scale (range / 255) and offset
00da3aab       (bias) are stored alongside the data. More precisely, the first 4 bytes
00da3af9       of each row in the output matrix are a 32-bit float storing the scale,
00da3b46       the next 4 bytes store the bias as a 32-bit float, and all remaining
00da3b91       bytes in the row encode single quantized values.
00da3bc8 Fused8BitRowwiseQuantizedToFloat
00da3bf0 De-quantizes the result of the
00da3c0f       FloatToFused8BitRowwiseQuantized operator. The input is expected to
00da3c59       encode the scale as a 32-bit float in the first 4 bytes of each row,
00da3ca4       followed by the bias as a 32-bit float in the next 4 bytes, followed by
00da3cf2       the quantized values in the remaining bytes of the row. The output is a
00da3d40       matrix containing only the values, but de-quantized. De-quantization is
00da3d8e       performed by multiplying each value by its row's scale and bias

00da4aa1 Hierarchical softmax is an operator which approximates the softmax operator
00da4aed while giving significant training speed gains and reasonably comparable
00da4b35 performance. In this operator, instead of calculating the probabilities of all
00da4b84 the classes, we calculate the probability of each step in the path from root to
00da4bd4 the target word in the hierarchy.
00da4bf7 The operator takes a 2-D tensor (Tensor<float>) containing a batch of layers, a
00da4c47 set of parameters represented by the weight matrix and bias terms, and a 1-D
00da4c94 tensor (Tensor<int>) holding labels, or the indices of the target class. The
00da4ce1 hierarchy has to be specified as an argument to the operator.
00da4d20 The operator returns a 1-D tensor holding the computed log probability of the
00da4d6e target class and a 2-D tensor of intermediate outputs (from the weight matrix
00da4dbc and softmax from each step in the path from root to target class) which will be
00da4e0c used by the gradient operator to compute gradients for all samples in the batch.

00da643c Given an input vector x \in [a_0, a_1, ...,a_{k-1}, a_k, ..., a_{n-1}],
00da6484 this op treats dimensions a_k through a_{n-1} as feature vectors. For each
00da64cf feature vector, the op contains the mean and standard deviation. Then,

00da7268 This operator applies 8Bit row-wise quantization to
00da729c     input tensor and returns quantized tensor. Row wise quantization of
00da72e4     input tensor is the following process. We take tensor of size
00da7326     (m_1, m_2,...,m_n), n >= 2, reshape it into matrix of size
00da7365     (m_1, m_2 x... x m_n) and apply row-wise quantization. After this,
00da73ac     we compute scale_i= (min_i - max_i) / 255 and  bias_i = min_i for
00da73f2     i-th row r_i of reshaped matrix, where min_i and max_i --  minimum
00da7439     and maximum elements of i-th row, and quantize each element r_{ij} as
00da7483     0 <= round(r_ij - bias_i) / scale_i) < 256. Instead of input tensor
00da74cb     we obtain uint8 tensor and auxiliary information as scale and bias to
00da7515     restore input tensor (with losses).
00da7540 Given uint8 tensor, quantized using 8bit row-wise
00da7572     quantization, and auxiliary scales and biases, this operator
00da75b3     restores float tensor in the following way. We take input 8bits tensor
00da75fe     of size  (m_1, m_2, ..., m_n), n >= 2, reshape it  into matrix of size
00da7649     (m_1, m_2 x... x m_n). We compute element r_{ij} of output matrix as
00da7692     r_{ij} * s_i + b_i and after this we reshape this output matrix into
00da76db     output tensor of size (m_1, m_2, ..., m_n).

00da979f feature. As described in https://caffe2.ai/docs/sparse-operations.html, a batch
00da97ef of ID_LIST examples is represented as a pair of lengths and values where the
00da983c `lengths` (int32) segment the `values` or ids (int32/int64) into examples.
00da9888 Given multiple inputs of the form lengths_0, values_0, lengths_1, values_1, ...
00da98d8 which correspond to lengths and values of ID_LISTs of different features, this
00da9927 operator produces a merged ID_LIST that combines the ID_LIST features. The
00da9972 final merged output is described by a lengths and values vector.
00da99b4 WARNING: The merge makes no guarantee about the relative order of ID_LISTs
00da99ff within a batch. This can be an issue if ID_LIST are order sensitive.

00db5050 /home/nshulga/git/caffe2/caffe2/operators/tt_linear_op.cc
00db5091 The TT-layer serves as a low-rank decomposition of a fully connected layer. The
00db50e1 inputs are the same as to a fully connected layer, but the number of parameters
00db5131 are greatly reduced and forward computation time can be drastically reduced
00db517d especially for layers with large weight matrices. The multiplication is computed
00db51ce as a product of the input vector with each of the cores that make up the TT
00db521a layer. Given the input sizes (inp_sizes), output sizes(out_sizes), and the ranks
00db526b of each of the cores (tt_ranks), the ith core will have size:
00db52aa     inp_sizes[i] * tt_ranks[i] * tt_ranks[i + 1] * out_sizes[i].
00db52ec The complexity of the computation is dictated by the sizes of inp_sizes,
00db5335 out_sizes, and tt_ranks, where there is the trade off between accuracy of the
00db5383 low-rank decomposition and the speed of the computation.

00db9b09 Learning rate is a decreasing function of time. With low learning rates the

00db9ba3 more exponential. Learning rate is controlled by the following arguments:
00db9bee #### Required
00db9bfd * `iterations`
00db9c0c * `base_lr`: base learning rate
00db9c2c * `policy`: this controls how the learning rate is applied, options are:
00db9c75   * `fixed`
00db9c81   * `step`: uses `stepsize`, `gamma`
00db9ca6   * `exp`: uses `gamma`
00db9cbe   * `inv`: uses `gamma`, `power`
00db9cdf   * `linearWarmup`: uses `start_multiplier`, `num_iter`
00db9d17   * `constantWarmup`: uses `multiplier`, `num_iter`
00db9d4b   * `alter`: uses  `active_first`, `active_period`, `inactive_period`
00db9d91   * `hill`: uses those in both `linearWarmup` and `inv`, plus `end_multiplier`
00db9de2 ### Optional:

00db9e5a * `start_multiplier`: defaults to 0

00dba0c2 Computes a momentum SGD update for an input gradient and momentum
00dba104 parameters. Concretely, given inputs (grad, m, lr) and parameters
00dba146 (momentum, nesterov), computes:

00dba17c         adjusted_gradient = lr * grad + momentum * m
00dba1b1         return (adjusted_gradient, adjusted_gradient)
00dba1e7     else:
00dba1f1         m_new = momentum * m + lr * grad
00dba21a         return ((1 + momentum) * m_new - momentum * m, m_new)

00dba2bb parameter update (and is thus faster).
00dba2e8 MomentumSGDUpdate
00dba302 Performs a momentum SGD update for an input gradient and momentum
00dba344 parameters. Concretely, given inputs (grad, m, lr, param) and arguments
00dba38c (momentum, nesterov), computes:
00dba3ad     if not nesterov:
00dba3c2         adjusted_gradient = lr * grad + momentum * m
00dba3f7         param = param - adjusted_gradient
00dba421         return (adjusted_gradient, adjusted_gradient, param)
00dba45e     else:
00dba468         m_new = momentum * m + lr * grad
00dba491         param = param - ((1 + momentum) * m_new - momentum * m),
00dba4d2         return ((1 + momentum) * m_new - momentum * m, m_new, param)

00dba6c8 RmsProp
